newsitem.title: IRAN: Turkmen gas line to Iran seen completed this year.
newsitem.headline: Turkmen gas line to Iran seen completed this year.

text.p: A pipeline supplying Turkmen gas to power plants in Northern Iran will be completed by the end of this year, the Iranian Petroleum Ministry's representative in Turkmenistan said on Monday.
The representative, Karim Tafreshi, was speaking on the sidelines of a gas conference.

The 200-km (130-mile) Korpedzhe-Kurt-Kuyi pipeline, the first new export line from the former Soviet Union not to pass through Russia, is expected to supply Iran with two billion cubic metres of Turkmen gas in its first year.

Iran's state-owned National Iranian Oil Industry and Engineering Company had completed 50 km of the 40-inch diameter line on Turkmenistan territory leaving a further 90 km to be constructed on Turkmen soil and 60 km on Iranian territory.
The $190 million pipeline deal is to be paid 80 percent by Turkmenistan through gas sales to Iran and 20 percent in cash, Tafreshi said.
The line is eventually planned to supply eight billion cubic metres a year in 10 years time.
First supplies to Iran have been scheduled for October.
